bearings.ref_pattern.measured_on: naming habit of one project; set it to how the bearing refs of your documents are named
bearings.ref_pattern.description: a body whose name (or whose component's name) matches is a candidate for a bearing, and so is one whose name carries a designation of the bearing table; its size is read from its geometry and must be a row of the table. A name alone stands only for a body with no ring geometry

bearings.clamp_room.measured_on: decided after both bearings of a built joint stayed loose with 0 to 0.3 mm of room (printed seats, steel washers under M3 screws, one printer, 0.6 nozzle); 1.0 itself is not confirmed by a print
bearings.clamp_room.description: the room for a clamped ring is shorter than the ring by this much, so the screws close on the ring and a gap stays open at the flange

bearings.cover_share_min.measured_on: decided: half the circle for a shoulder or lip; not measured
bearings.cover_share_min.description: share of a ring-face circle a shoulder or lip must cover to count as holding that face

bearings.clamp_points_min.measured_on: owner decision of one project: six washers per ring where they fit, never under four; three beside a connector slot was a named exception
bearings.clamp_points_min.description: separate clamps (steel washers under screws) round a ring face that hold it instead of a full shoulder

bearings.contact_gap_max.measured_on: decided: modelling tolerance of a touching face
bearings.contact_gap_max.description: a part farther than this from a ring face does not hold it

bearings.seat_d_tol.measured_on: decided: covers a seat tapered by 0.25 on the diameter at its entry; not measured
bearings.seat_d_tol.description: largest difference between a seat diameter and the bearing diameter it holds

bearings.pass_clearance.measured_on: decided after a bearing could not pass a ring 1.2 mm under its outer diameter; the 0.2 was never measured
bearings.pass_clearance.description: radial clearance to the bearing of everything it passes on the way to its seat

bearings.clamp_plastic_max.measured_on: decided: printed plastic under a clamp load creeps; one project accepted about 4 mm in one joint as a named exception
bearings.clamp_plastic_max.description: printed plastic allowed between the head of a clamp screw and the ring it clamps

bearings.seat_taper.measured_on: owner decision of one project (one printer, 0.6 nozzle, PETG); the fit of a seat tapered this way is not yet measured
bearings.seat_taper.description: a printed bore seat is nominal at the stop where the ring ends up and this much wider on the diameter at its mouth; a printed post is nominal where the ring enters and this much wider towards the shoulder that stops it (bearings.seat_taper_thick_base beside a thick base). bearings.seat judges a bore by this number

bearings.seat_taper_thick_base.measured_on: one printed post measured 0.5 mm smaller on the diameter beside its thick base than at its free end (one printer, 0.6 nozzle, PETG); as a compensation it is decided, never printed
bearings.seat_taper_thick_base.description: compensation on the diameter for the part of a seat that sits right beside a thick base, until the first print is measured; bearings.seat takes it as the most a post may widen from the end the ring enters to its stop

bearings.seat_lead_in.description: leg of the 45 degree chamfer at the mouth of a bearing seat

bearings.lip_min.measured_on: owner decision of one project (one printer, 0.6 nozzle); small gearbox parts of the same project kept 1.0, decided and not measured
bearings.lip_min.description: least thickness of a printed lip or shoulder that holds a ring face

bearings.other_ring_relief.description: a hub or shoulder that carries one ring stands back from the other ring and the seal by this much along the axis

bearings.axial_free_gap.measured_on: decided (0.3 to 0.5 was in use) after a closed axial loop met a bought unit that was 0.4 mm off its drawing; not measured
bearings.axial_free_gap.description: open axial gap at the stack of a bearing pair that does not set the length

bearings.shaft_under_bore.measured_on: owner decision of one project after hardened pins of the nominal bore size did not enter the bearings
bearings.shaft_under_bore.description: a bought shaft or pin through a bearing is this much smaller than the bore and carries a printed sleeve

bearings.sleeve_axial_play.description: axial play of a printed sleeve between the two parts that close it in

bearings.clamp_room_washer.measured_on: the value of bearings.clamp_room before the two were split; a washer that closes 1.0 past the ring face tilted about 6 degrees on one print (one printer, 0.6 nozzle), so a project sets its own washer room (tag M or U)
bearings.clamp_room_washer.description: the room for a ring clamped by a steel washer: the landing beside the ring is set back from the ring face by at least this much, so the washer closes on the ring (washers.landing reads it)

bearings.seat_form.measured_on: decided: "any" keeps the nominal and the tapered seat both; a project whose printed seats are all tapered sets "tapered" (an owner decision)
bearings.seat_form.description: any | tapered: with "tapered" every printed seat of a bearing is a tapered press fit, and a straight seat fails bearings.seat

bearings.seat_taper_tol.measured_on: decided, not printed: the grid a seat profile is measured to (0.01) is finer; 0.05 is the least that tells 0.25 from 0.5
bearings.seat_taper_tol.description: how far the widening of a tapered seat may be off bearings.seat_taper or bearings.seat_taper_thick_base

bearings.sleeve_pattern.measured_on: decided, not measured: the words a printed sleeve or spacer is named with. Set it to how the project names them
bearings.sleeve_pattern.description: a printed part whose name matches is a sleeve or a spacer: its end is never the clamp or the stop of a bearing ring (bearings.sleeve_end_and_preload)

rules.title: Every bearing ring is held on both faces
rules.statement: Bearings are found, not listed. A name picks the candidates (the bearing pattern, or a designation of the bearing table in the name of a body or of its component); the geometry decides: a ring whose d, D and B are a row of the table is that bearing, and a body that measures otherwise than the row its name carries is not a bearing. A ring that only misses its row (two of d, D and B fit: the model of the bought part is off), and a ring the probe passed over, is not judged and not passed: the check is not run for it until the model or the table is corrected. Each ring of each bearing (inner and outer) is held along the axis on both faces, four contacts per bearing, by something that touches only that ring: a printed shoulder or lip over at least {bearings.cover_share_min} of the ring-face circle, or at least {bearings.clamp_points_min} separate clamps (steel washers under screws) round it, each within {bearings.contact_gap_max} of the face. A press fit alone holds no ring. A cover that touches both rings fails; the other bearing of a pair, ring on ring, is no such cover. A bearing with no table row or no ring geometry is never skipped: the check is not run until the row is added or the ref is a ring. A ring is judged with the part that seats it or holds one of its faces. A bearing that bought bodies hold and at whose rings no printed part stands, seats or clamps (the rollers inside a bought gearbox) is not a finding of a printed part that is screwed to that assembly: one row per part tells how many and which, and names the mesh bodies near them. A printed lip or clamp that stops short of a ring face answers for that face, however far off it stands. A bearing that nothing touches at all stays a finding of every part near it. A ring that is free on purpose is a named exception: an owner waiver on this rule.
rules.why: Bearings were modelled with no retention at all. A shoulder touched the turning ring. A 2 mm printed retainer carried a whole joint on four weak inserts. Bearings and their clamps lived in hand-typed tables inside a script: a new bearing was invisible to every check until someone added a row.
fix_order: Add a printed shoulder or lip on the open face: on that ring only, past the ring chamfer (the bearing table gives the least shoulder diameters).
Where a shoulder cannot be printed or assembled, add steel washers under screws next to the ring, spread round the circle.
A cover that touches both rings: relieve it over the other ring and the seal.
A bearing with no table row: add its size to the bearing table. A bearing the gate did not find at all: name its ref so the pattern matches.
A ring that is free on purpose (a floating bearing against one lip, an idler pair on its bolt): owner waiver that names the bearing and what closes it.

rules.title: A clamped ring has clamp room
rules.statement: The axial room between the two stops of a clamped ring is shorter than the ring by at least {bearings.clamp_room} for a printed clamp and {bearings.clamp_room_washer} for a steel washer clamp: the screws close on the ring, not on the plastic, and a visible gap stays open at the flange. The same holds for a spacer clamped between two rings. Clamp screws sit next to the ring. The open gap is counted in every stack above it. A ring is clamped when two bodies touch its two faces (each within {bearings.contact_gap_max}); a body that only stands near a face clamps nothing, and bearings.holding fails that face.
rules.why: Both bearings of a built joint stayed loose however hard the screws were tightened: the seats had 0 to 0.3 mm of clamp room. Printed shims and a longer spacer patched the printed parts. The cut that made the room was driven by two hand tables and nothing measured the result.
fix_order: Set the landing of the clamp (washer landing or cover face) back from the ring face by the clamp room.
A spacer clamped between two rings: make the room for it shorter than the spacer by the clamp room too.
Add the open gap to every stack above it: screw lengths and the height of whatever sits on the flange.
Run the insert and relief checks of the part again: a landing cut can remove a melt relief or thin a wall, and it moves the hardware refs.
A part that is already printed: a shim of the missing room under the clamp, recorded as a bench patch; the model is fixed all the same.
rules.note: A clamp of bought bodies on a bearing with no printed part at its rings (a steel washer on a roller inside a bought gearbox) is not judged for the printed part beside it: bearings.holding tells those bearings in one row. A clamp row that names a printed part, touching or not, keeps the bearing judged. The ring width is the measured width of the batch in hand when the project records it (gate/owner/tables.json "bearings": "measured"), else the width of the ref body.

rules.title: One stack of a bearing pair has room
rules.statement: Between two bearings on one axis only one stack (the inner rings or the outer rings) carries a fixed length that touches both rings. The other stack leaves at least {bearings.clamp_room} of room at its rings, so its second ring has no hard stop and the spacer alone sets the distance. Two fixed lengths between one pair of rings cannot both be tight.
rules.why: A built joint had an inner-ring spacer and a tube shoulder-to-spigot length, both drawn 45.0: the spacer rattled with about 2 mm of room, also with a shim. Nothing measured the two stacks against each other.
fix_order: Name the stack that sets the distance (usually the spacer between the inner rings).
Move the second stop of the other stack back by the clamp room: the seat floor under the second outer ring 1.0 deeper, or the tube shoulder 1.0 shorter.
A part that is already printed: a longer spacer on the bench (the measured room plus the clamp room), recorded as the owner's decision.
rules.note: Judged from the covers the bearing unit lists on the facing ring faces of the two bearings (every body within 2 mm, with its gap). A stack body that never comes within 2 mm of a ring face is no stop. A mesh or hidden body near the pair makes a pass NOT_RUN.

rules.title: A seat fits its bearing
rules.statement: Every bearing sits in a seat of its own size: the seat diameter where the ring ends up differs from the bearing diameter (bore for a seat on a post, outer diameter for a seat in a housing) by at most {bearings.seat_d_tol}, or the seat is a tapered press fit: a post nominal (within that tolerance) at the end the ring enters and at most {bearings.seat_taper_thick_base} wider towards the shoulder that stops it, a bore nominal at its stop and at most {bearings.seat_taper} wider towards its mouth, measured end by end; the way into the seat is not in the bearing's way by more than that; and every bearing-sized seat of the part holds a bearing. Sizes come from the bearing table; a size or formula copied from another bearing is evaluated again. Every bought bearing exists as a named ref body in each document that uses it. A seat with a bought body on its axis that no pattern recognised is not called empty: the check is not run until the body is named. A hole that is only near a bearing diameter is asked, not failed. With {bearings.seat_form} "tapered" a straight seat fails, a taper fails unless its widening is {bearings.seat_taper} or {bearings.seat_taper_thick_base} within {bearings.seat_taper_tol}, and a seat whose entry end has no {bearings.seat_lead_in} x 45 degree lead-in (measured where the seat wall ends) fails. With "any", a straight seat more than {bearings.seat_taper_tol} off its bearing is shown as INFO. A seat fit counts only where it was printed: when the seat fit of the bearings table records prints, a seat of a part whose declared target is none of them fails as "measured under other settings". A through hole thinner than the bearing it would seat is asked, not called an empty seat.
rules.why: A formula copied from another bearing size left a ring 1.2 mm under the outer diameter in the way: the bearing could not reach its seat and the lid was reprinted. One copy of a bearing ref stayed 2 mm off after the bearing moved. Seats were compared with their bearings by a hand table of eight rows.
fix_order: Take d, D and B from the bearing table of the rules (tables/bearings.json).
Evaluate again every size that was copied from another bearing.
An entry that is in the way: widen everything the bearing passes to its own diameter and more (bearings.insertion_path).
A seat with no bearing in it: place the bearing ref (in every document that uses the bearing), or remove the seat.
A seat that is tapered or compensated beyond the taper parameters on purpose: the project raises them with a measured or owner value, never the agent.
rules.note: The seat of a bearing that bought bodies hold and at whose rings no printed part stands, seats or clamps (a roller on a steel post) is not this part's seat: not judged here, bearings.holding tells those bearings in one row.

rules.title: A bearing can reach its seat
rules.statement: Everything a bearing passes on the way to its seat clears it by {bearings.pass_clearance} on the radius: larger than its outer diameter in a housing, smaller than its bore on a post. That includes a ring, a lip or the seat of another bearing that lies on the way. A formula copied from another bearing size is evaluated again. Measured on the body that seats the ring, over the stretch beyond the ring face on its more open side: a wall there is the seat itself (within {bearings.seat_d_tol}, or the band of a tapered seat) or it clears the ring.
rules.why: A bearing could not pass a ring 1.2 mm under its outer diameter and never reached its seat; the printed lid was thrown away. The ring came from a formula written for a smaller bearing.
fix_order: Widen everything between the seat mouth and the seat to the bearing diameter plus the pass clearance.
Move the narrow ring behind the seat, or make it a separate part fitted after the bearing.
Put the bearing in from the other side.
rules.note: Judged from the seat facts of fusion_bearings: "entry_d" is the narrowest (housing) or widest (post) diameter of the seat body beyond the ring face on the side the ring comes from ("entry_side"), over the width of the ring, 6 to 20 mm; "entry_open" says nothing of that body stands there. A seat whose entry is narrower than the ring by more than the seat tolerance is a row of bearings.seat (it cannot reach the seat at all); this rule fails the walls that are not the seat and stand closer than the pass clearance. Not measured: a lip of ANOTHER part on the way, farther out than that stretch.

rules.title: No printed plastic in a bearing clamp stack
rules.statement: Between the head of a clamp screw and the ring it clamps there is steel only: the washer and the ring. At most {bearings.clamp_plastic_max} of printed plastic lies in that stack: plastic under a clamp load creeps and the clamp loosens. A longer standard screw is no reason to put plastic into the stack.
rules.why: One clamp ran through about 4 mm of a printed part and was accepted once, as an exception, with the order to tighten it again after the first hours. The longer standard screw would have put 17 mm of plastic into the same clamp.
fix_order: Seat the washer on the ring and the screw head on the washer.
Thread the clamp screw into the part the ring sits in, next to the ring, so nothing printed lies under the head.
Plastic that must stay in the stack: owner waiver with its thickness, and a retighten step in the build notes.
rules.note: Judged from the clamp facts of fusion_bearings: a clamp row whose clamping body ("name", "by": "printed") is a printed part puts that part between the screw heads and the ring. One FAIL per ring; only the owner waives it (with the thickness and a retighten step in the build notes). A printed sleeve or spacer in the clamp path is bearings.sleeve_end_and_preload, not a row here. The stop on the other face may be printed: it takes the load in compression, it is not in the screw stack.

rules.title: A bearing that is not clamped is a named exception
rules.statement: A bearing that is not held on four ring faces is an exception with a name: a floating bearing against one lip, an idler pair on its bolt, a bearing captured in the print, the bearings inside a bought unit or inside a sub-assembly that has its own document. Each one has an owner waiver on bearings.holding that names the bearing, what holds it instead and why that is enough. An exception that stands only in a comment of a tool is not named.
rules.why: The exceptions of one project were listed only in the docstring of a cutting script. The question whether one outer ring, held by a single lip, was held well enough stayed open for weeks.
fix_order: Run the gate on every document that holds bearings, the sub-assembly documents too.
Propose a waiver per free ring; the owner accepts or rejects it.

rules.title: A sleeve end takes no clamp load
rules.statement: The end of a printed sleeve or thin spacer never takes the clamp load of a bearing: the clamp closes on steel. Preload screws are tightened evenly and only until the play is gone. A ring is pressed home only through the ring that is being fitted, never through the balls.
rules.why: No print was lost to this yet. It is written from how the parts fail: a one-line sleeve end crushes under a clamp and the bearing ends up loose; force through the balls dents the races.
fix_order: Let the sleeve end short of the clamped faces: it has axial play.
Clamp the rings against a steel spacer, a shoulder of the shaft or washers.
rules.note: Judged from the clamp facts of fusion_bearings: a clamp row whose clamping body or stop ("against") is a printed part named like a sleeve or spacer (bearings.sleeve_pattern) puts the sleeve end in the clamp path: FAIL. The name only adds a row, it never takes one away. Preload and pressing are not measured.

rules.title: A bearing captured in the print
rules.statement: A bearing that is laid into a paused print (print-in): layers do not stick to steel, so the layer over the bearing needs plastic beside it to land on; the pause height lies on the layer grid; two parts whose lips face each other cannot be assembled round a captured bearing. Prefer a bearing that slides on after printing.
rules.why: A print-in bearing failed: the layers over it did not stick to the steel and the lips of the two parts faced each other. The design went to slide-on bearings.
fix_order: Make the bearing slide on after printing, held by a lip on one face and a clamp on the other.
Where it must be captured: put the pause on a layer boundary and give the first layer over it plastic to land on.

rules.title: A printed seat is tapered, and shrinks beside a thick base
rules.statement: A printed bearing seat is a tapered press fit with a lead-in. A post (inner ring) is nominal at the end the ring enters and {bearings.seat_taper} wider on the diameter at the shoulder that stops it ({bearings.seat_taper_thick_base} beside a thick base); a bore (outer ring) is nominal at its stop and {bearings.seat_taper} wider at its mouth. Where the ring enters, the seat ends in a {bearings.seat_lead_in} x 45 degree chamfer: at the free end of a post, at the mouth of a bore. The part of a seat right beside a thick base shrinks more as it cools: compensate it by {bearings.seat_taper_thick_base} until the first print is measured, then use the measured value. Zones another ring must pass stay clear of the taper. A compensation above {bearings.seat_d_tol} needs that tolerance raised in the project with a measured or owner value.
rules.why: A heavy base was printed with a bearing post that measured nominal at its free end and 0.5 mm small at the disc: the lower bearing rocked on it. An older rule said seats are modelled nominal and the fit is left to the slicer.
fix_order: Measure the first print at both ends of the seat and write the result as a measured project parameter.
Print the seat zone as a small coupon before the big part when the part is heavy.
rules.note: Supersedes "seats are modelled nominal, the fit is the slicer's compensation": that still holds only for the part of a seat away from a thick base.

rules.title: One stack sets a bearing pair
rules.statement: In an arrangement of two bearings exactly one stack sets the length, for example the inner rings through a spacer. The other ring pair has no second hard stop: it keeps an open gap of {bearings.axial_free_gap} or slides. A part has one axial datum. Where two load paths meet across a bearing, one of them is a sliding fit with an open gap sized from the measured bought part.
rules.why: A printed joint did not go together: a closed axial loop through the bearing met a bought gear unit that was 0.4 mm off its drawing. Three parts were reprinted. A tube was printed with a second stop under the ring.
fix_order: Name the stack that sets the length and remove the second stop.
Measure the bought unit before the gap is sized.

rules.title: A shoulder touches one ring
rules.statement: A shoulder or hub beside a bearing touches exactly one ring. Its band lies on that ring's face, past the ring chamfer (the bearing table gives the least shoulder diameters), and it stands back from the other ring and the seal by {bearings.other_ring_relief} along the axis. A lip that holds a ring is at least {bearings.lip_min} thick and follows the minimum wall; where that does not fit, pick a narrower bearing. A flat ledge that faces down in the print is not a shoulder: it cannot be printed.
rules.why: A 1 mm inner-ring shoulder was modelled as a flat ledge that faced down: it could not be printed. Another shoulder touched the turning ring.
fix_order: Narrow the shoulder to the band of its own ring.
Print the shoulder as part of an upward-opening seat, or make it a separate ring.
Pick a narrower or smaller bearing when the lip cannot reach its thickness.

rules.title: A seat prints as a cylinder that opens upward
rules.statement: A bearing seat prints as a vertical cylinder that opens upward, with no support inside it. If the layers are then loaded badly, keep the seat orientation and add material.
rules.why: A cam was printed on its side for layer strength: the seat sagged, the bearing did not go on, the part was reprinted upright.
fix_order: Turn the part so the seat axis is the print axis.
Add material where the layers are loaded across; do not turn the seat on its side.

rules.title: A bought shaft through a bearing carries a printed sleeve
rules.statement: A bought shaft or pin through a bearing is {bearings.shaft_under_bore} smaller than the bore and carries a printed sleeve with {bearings.sleeve_axial_play} of axial play. A shaft of the nominal bore size is bought only after its tolerance class is read: an m6 pin does not enter a bore of the same nominal size. Its length is checked against the pocket measured on the exported part, and only ready lengths are bought. The sleeve is a one-line wall: its two diameters come from a fit ladder (walls.one_line). A bought shaft that seats the inner ring itself (no printed sleeve between) at less than {bearings.shaft_under_bore} under the bore fails.
rules.why: Hardened pins of the nominal bore size did not enter the bearings and were 6 mm too long for their pocket: the money was wasted and the pins were ordered again.
fix_order: Read the tolerance class and the real length of the bought shaft before the order.
Size the sleeve from the fit ladder, not from the model.
rules.note: Judged from the seat facts of fusion_bearings: the inner ring seated on a bought or hardware body ("seat"."inner"."kind") of diameter "d". A shaft of the nominal bore size (m6 is over it) fails, and so does any bought shaft closer to the bore than bearings.shaft_under_bore: the room is the printed sleeve. A bearing that bought bodies hold and no printed part does (a roller on a steel post inside a bought gearbox) is not judged for a printed part. The sleeve itself and the length of the shaft against its pocket are fits.bought_part_pocket.
